items.title: Antigravity details how Gemini 4 Argon ported a 174K-line Fortran ocean model's core to safe Rust in 59 minutes, and ships the workflow as a skill
items.summary: Google's write-up of one agent run on FVCOM (174,774 lines of Fortran and C across 264 files). From one prompt with hard rules (no unsafe code, no heap allocations in hot loops, files under 400 lines, 95% branch coverage, bit-level parity over 100 seeds), the agent captured a gfortran baseline, wrote a blueprint, rewrote the core solver as 13 Rust modules, and self-fixed one failing test. It reports 100 of 100 seeds matching to about 4e-13, six real bugs found in the old code, and runtime going from 883 ms to 469 ms (1.88x) with 54% less memory after a PGO pass. The workflow is released as an open-source /migrate-to-rust skill in Google's skills repo.

doubt.pushback: Vendor's own showcase run. The port covers the core solver (13 modules), not all 174K lines, and the timings come from one benchmark harness built by the agent.

items.reception: Deep read of the blog post. Engagement is steady (345 likes, 32 reposts) with no pushback seen in the window.

items.title: vLLM v0.33.0: Reflection Beam-1.0, Step-5 Preview and MiniCPM-OCR support, PyTorch 2.14 on CUDA 13 wheels, faster GB300 decode
items.summary: A large release (927 commits, 389 contributors). New models include Reflection Beam-1.0, Step-5 Preview, Nemotron Parse 3.5 and MiniCPM-OCR 1.0. It moves to PyTorch 2.14 with CUDA 13.0-only wheels, adds speculative decoding options (XPress refiner, FLy lossy verify at 1.04 to 1.31x), reports DSpark going from 1373 to 3390 tok/s and 1.5 to 2x faster decode on GB300, and makes ROCm 10.0 the default. CUDA 13-only wheels matter for anyone pinning vLLM on older drivers, including the DGX Spark.

items.title: GLM-5.3 753B runs at about 70 tok/s single-stream on four DGX Sparks with a published TensorFold TP4 recipe
items.summary: Using the author's 3.38 bpw SAGE-EXL3 quant (all 19,200 experts in 319 GB), @cfontes's TensorFold TP4 plus DFlash2 recipe measures p50 single-request speeds of 69.2 tok/s on code, 55.7 on prose and 73.6 on structured output with a 1M context configured. Prefix caching cut a sixth agent turn (15,930 tokens) from 85.3 s cold to 19.4 s. The quant matched BF16's next token 93% of the time with 2.1% higher perplexity. Both the recipe and the weights are published.

doubt.pushback: Numbers come from the quant's own author, and the comparison figures from other recipes used different harnesses.

items.title: Spark-X2.6-4B Q8 holds 288K context at about 67 tok/s on a single 12 GB RTX 3060
items.summary: A llama-server config (q8_0 KV cache, flash attention) runs the 4B model with 288K context at about 67 tok/s decode and 3,500 tok/s prefill, and finds a needle at 280K. Only 9 of its 36 layers keep a full KV cache, which is why long context is cheap. Switching the KV cache to q4_0 reaches 448K on the same card with the needle still found at 436K, though decode falls to about 12 tok/s that deep. The full command line is in the post.
items.reception: Posted 2026-11-02 but surfaced in this window through a quote by the model's maker @SparkLLM.

items.title: Fable hand-writes the weights of a 100K-parameter legal citation classifier that beats a trained version
items.summary: Legora's CTO says Fable wrote every weight of a 100K-parameter network that tells real legal citations from fake ones, in one shot, and that it scores better than training the same network. It follows this week's weight-space programming results (Hugging Face's repro was kept on 2026-11-03), now applied to a small production-style task.

doubt.pushback: Single screenshot with no code, dataset or eval details yet, so the better-than-training claim is unchecked.

items.reception: Widely shared (about 4,800 likes, 197 reposts, 129 quotes). Quotes are mostly excitement. @carterleffen quoted it with his own attempt a few hours later, @Alex_tra_memory posted a legal citation checker he says Claude wrote weight by weight, and @omarsar0 calls weight-space programming the most exciting research he has seen lately. No refutation seen.

items.title: OpenAI shows ChatGPT and Codex working on mechanical design, electrical engineering and simulation
items.summary: OpenAI shared progress using ChatGPT and Codex for physical engineering, from speeding up its own hardware teams to testing workflows with industry partners, with a focus on mechanical design, electrical engineering and simulation. Greg Brockman framed it as letting amateurs design prototype devices.
items.reception: Posted 18:56Z, before this window, and missed by the 19:09 sweep; surfaced through @gdb quotes. About 5,200 likes and 414 reposts. The attached video (about 80 s) was not watched.

items.title: Vals: four of seven frontier models keep 80% of their score at the lowest reasoning effort for half the cost or less
items.summary: Vals ran seven frontier models at three reasoning levels across the Vals Index. Four kept at least 80% of their performance at the lowest setting while costing half as much or less, which supports defaulting agents to lower effort and raising it only where it pays.

items.title: Artificial Analysis Capability Indexes v2.0 weight hallucination and agentic tool use more
items.summary: The six occupation indexes (Finance and Accounting, Strategy and Ops, Legal, Healthcare, Engineering, Economics) now align with Intelligence Index v5.0. Changes include more weight on Non-Hallucination and Agentic Tool Use, HLE upgraded to HLE-Diamond, AA-Omniscience to v1.1, GDPval-AA dropped from agentic knowledge work, and a new Science capability for Engineering from CritPt v2 and Terminal-Bench-Science, plus FrontierCode 2.0 in agentic coding.

security_forwarded.matched: stack: docker (match_terms container escape, seccomp); always_forward: container runtimes and images.
security_forwarded.summary: CVE-2026-112917 (CVSS 4.0 9.2): on Docker Desktop for Windows with the WSL 2 backend on x86-64, an unprivileged container can use 32-bit socketcall to get around the default seccomp block on AF_VSOCK and reach host services and the user's Windows files. Fixed only with Docker Desktop 4.98.0 (released 2026-11-03) plus WSL 3.0.3 or later, then wsl --shutdown. Docker Engine on Linux (the Spark, cspie), Mac, ARM and Hyper-V backends are not affected. The only possible exposure is csdesktop if it runs Docker Desktop on WSL 2, which nobody has checked.
